sessionTitle: Build and deploy AI at the edge for real-world impact

announcements.name: Azure Local capabilities for small form factor devices (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Cloud-based provisioning and management functions previously limited to large Azure Local servers are now available in preview for compact industrial hardware
announcements.longDescription: Capabilities that Microsoft Azure has offered for several years, such as provisioning machines from the cloud and managing them from the cloud, were previously limited to Azure Local on big servers. What's new is that those same capabilities are now available in preview for smaller industrial form factors. This small form factor infrastructure was the industrial computer used to run the demo.

announcements.name: Cloud provisioning without local peripherals
announcements.shortDescription: Using an ownership voucher in the Azure portal, a device can have its software stack (e.g., Azure Linux) installed straight from the cloud with no keyboard or monitor attached
announcements.longDescription: In the Azure portal, a machine can be provisioned by inputting the ownership voucher for a Lenovo SE100 device, which the portal then picks up. The user can choose which software stack to install onto the computer straight from the cloud portal without needing to plug in a keyboard or monitor; in this case Azure Linux was chosen and provisioned entirely from the cloud. This produces a provisioned machine resource representation in Azure Resource Manager that looks and works much like a cloud virtual machine, including management functions such as granting access to a colleague via Microsoft Entra ID.
